title: Reconnected
content:
As Sneha stepped out of the company building, her eyes once again fell upon the small slip of paper in her hand.

Rohini.

The name lingered in her mind.

Could she be the same Rohini Siddu had mentioned during their journey?

Unable to ignore her curiosity, Sneha walked toward the cab waiting outside the building and immediately dialled the number.

The phone rang for a few moments before a gentle female voice answered.

"Hello, this is Rohini speaking. May I know who's calling?"

Sneha quickly replied,

"Hello, ma'am. I'm Sneha... your new teammate. I was informed that I'll be working under your guidance from tomorrow."

"Oh! That's wonderful," Rohini said warmly. "Welcome to the team."

"Thank you, ma'am."

There was a brief pause before Sneha gathered the courage to ask,

"Ma'am... if you don't mind, are you from Bengaluru?"

"Yes," Rohini replied. "I am."

Sneha's heartbeat quickened.

"Then... do you happen to know someone named Siddharth from Bengaluru?"

For a moment, there was complete silence.

When Rohini finally spoke, surprise was evident in her voice.

"Siddharth? Of course I know him. He's one of my closest friends."

A wave of excitement rushed through Sneha.

Trying to control her emotions, she immediately said,

"Ma'am, I met him during my train journey from Kochi to Delhi. Before he could finish telling me something important, he suddenly left the train without informing me. I've been trying to contact him ever since."

Rohini listened quietly.

For a few moments, neither of them spoke.

Rohini seemed to be thinking carefully.

"So..." she finally said. "You met Siddharth on a train, and ever since then you've been searching for him?"

"Yes, ma'am," Sneha replied honestly. "I know it sounds strange. We were complete strangers when we met. But during that journey, he shared a part of his life with me. Before he could finish his story, he suddenly disappeared without telling me anything."

Rohini remained silent, listening to every word.

"There was something in his eyes," Sneha continued softly. "He looked like someone carrying a pain he had never shared with anyone. I don't know why... but after he left, I couldn't stop thinking about him. I just want to know if he's alright."

A gentle smile appeared on Rohini's face.

"That sounds exactly like Siddharth," she said with a faint laugh. "He always carries everyone's burdens by himself. No matter how much pain he's in, he never lets others see it."

Sneha listened carefully.

"You know," Rohini continued, "he has helped many people without expecting anything in return. But when it comes to sharing his own problems, he simply walks away."

Sneha lowered her eyes for a moment.

"So... he really is that kind of person."

"He is," Rohini replied. "That's why I wanted to be sure before giving you his number. Nowadays, we can't simply share someone's personal contact with a stranger."

"I completely understand, ma'am," Sneha said politely. "Thank you for trusting me."

Rohini smiled softly.

"From the way you've spoken about him, I can tell your intentions are genuine."

She unlocked her phone and opened her contact list.

"Alright," she said. "Just give me a moment."

After scrolling for a few seconds, she found the contact.

"Here it is," she said, slowly reading out Siddharth's phone number.

Sneha carefully saved the contact on her phone.

"Thank you so much, ma'am," she said gratefully. "I really appreciate your help."

"It's alright," Rohini replied. "I'll see you tomorrow at the office."

The call ended.

As the cab moved through the busy streets of Delhi, Sneha's eyes repeatedly drifted toward the newly saved contact on her phone.

Siddharth.

After days of unanswered questions and endless searching, she finally had a way to reach him.

Her heart pounded with excitement.

What would she say?

Would he recognize her?

Would he even answer the call?

Standing quietly near the window of her room, she stared at the screen. Her thumb hovered over the call button for a few seconds before she finally gathered the courage to press it.

The ringtone echoed through the silence.

Once.

Twice.

Then...

The call connected.

For a heartbeat, neither of them spoke.

"Hello..."

The familiar voice from the other end sent a wave of emotions rushing through Sneha.

It was Siddu.
